approach: Add `check_behavior_test_reading` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, gated by the existing `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`. Wire it as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in checks.rs. The four parts are matched lexically on labelled assumptions: `Gate order:` (a), `Existing code:` (b, the label the codebase already uses), `Record kind:` (c) and `Direct check:` (d). One generic `assumptions_labeled` helper replaces the three copies of the label filter (`code_surveys`, `environment_assumptions`, `existing_code_assumptions`). The check gathers every missing or contradicting part into one error that names the parts and the check, so the `refuse:` line of `athena check-reading` shows it. Skip-switch matching uses a closed, documented list, so legitimate names such as `skip_note` pass. A negator counts only directly before the switch. A single-word entry point counts when backticked or written `name()`. The routine-criterion test strips flag tokens and crate names before it checks a stop list. AC4 is measured on real readings by the producer loop's `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) and by the verification replay. The fixture replay test covers mechanics only. The producer reports `status.rs`, `verify.rs` and `replay.rs` in `unchanged_planned_files`. No prompt file, record, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow is touched.

decisions.choice: Part (b) is satisfied by an `Existing code:` assumption (found with `existing_code_assumptions`) that names a `crates/` path the job does not create (`names_existing_path` over the created paths) and holds one code identifier. No `Reuses:` label is added. Parts (a), (c) and (d) use the new labels `Gate order:`, `Record kind:` and `Direct check:`. A new generic `assumptions_labeled(reading, label)` helper is added, and `code_surveys`, `environment_assumptions` and `existing_code_assumptions` are rewritten to call it.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. `existing_code_assumptions` (surveys.rs:1329-1336) already parses `Existing code:`, and `check_design_existing_code` uses it for reuse. A reading that states reuse the usual way must not be refused for (b). Fewer new labels also means a smaller newly refused share. Three copies of the same filter (surveys.rs:117-124, 605-612, 1329-1336) become one function, so there is no fourth copy.

rejected.option: Add a new `Reuses:` label, with or without `Existing code:` as an alias
rejected.why: A reading that already states reuse under `Existing code:` would be refused for a label no past reading used. That raises the refused share for no gain.

rejected.option: Look for the four parts as free prose in the `Code survey:` text
rejected.why: Prose cannot tell the error which part is missing, and AC2 needs the missing part named.

decisions.choice: Part (a) needs a `Gate order:` body with at least two code identifiers and a stop-gate phrase (`stop gate`, `stops at`, `stops after`, `stop at`, `stops before`). An identifier is any of: a token with `_` or `::`, a backticked token, or a word directly followed by `()`. Tokens with `/` or a file extension never count. Part (c) needs a `Record kind:` body that satisfies `names_record_evidence`, or `none` when no deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`, or a deliverable path whose file name holds `round_trip`, `roundtrip` or `round-trip`. `none` beside a record or data deliverable with no round-trip test deliverable is refused as a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Finding 5. Real entry points are often one word, such as `replay` (replay.rs:365). `Gate order: `replay` then `check_reading_text`; stops at `replay`` holds two backticked identifiers and passes. The record rule is decided from the deliverable list alone, which the existing check also does (surveys.rs:217-230), so no repository read is needed.

rejected.why: A single-word entry point or gate never counts, so correct readings would be refused.
A new record file with `none` is the contradiction AC3 requires the check to refuse.

decisions.choice: Part (d): each non-routine behavior criterion must be named `criterion N` in a `Direct check:` body, and that body must hold at least one identifier (same definition as in (a)). A skip switch is matched by a closed list: the exact names `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, plus upper-case env-var tokens that start `ATHENA_NO_` or `ATHENA_SKIP_` (case-sensitive). Lower-case identifiers that merely contain `skip_` or `_skip` are never matched. An internal-helper read is matched by the phrases `internal helper`, `private helper`, `stand-in`, `through a helper` and `via a helper`. A match is refused unless negated. A negator counts only when it is the token directly before the match, or directly before one connective (`through`, `via`, `using`, `with`, `by`, `of`) that is directly before the match. Negators are `no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nor`, `avoid`, `avoiding`, `instead`, `than`. The Limits text and the CHANGELOG state the closed list. They also state that another name, or a switch described in prose, is not caught. They pin one false case: `no probe runs when skip_probe is set` is refused, because the negator is not directly before the switch.
decisions.reason: Findings 2 and 7. A Grep by the critic found 208 `skip_`/`_skip` identifiers in 43 files, including the production function `skip_note` (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs:271). A direct check that calls `skip_note` is legitimate. `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` come from the request, and AC3 names them. A closed list is testable and its limit can be stated. A four-token negation window accepted `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, so the window is replaced by the directly-before rule. The reading checks read the Reading only, with no repository (surveys.rs:310-311), so the list cannot be checked against the code.

rejected.why: It refuses real function names such as `skip_note`.
`no` or `than` anywhere in the window accepts a mention that is not negated.

rejected.option: Detect switches by reading the repository
rejected.why: The reading checks have no repository access.

decisions.choice: A criterion is routine, and needs no direct check, when after stripping every whitespace token that starts with `-` (flags such as `-p`, `-D`, `--all-targets`, `--locked`) and every token that starts `athena-` (crate names), the remaining words, split on non-alphanumerics and lower-cased, are all in a stop list. The stop list is: cargo, fmt, clippy, test, tests, check, pass, passes, passing, and, the, on, final, tree, still, all, locked, same, as, a, recorded, athena, workspace, warnings, targets, no, unrelated, behavior, changes, change, existing, run. The criterion must also hold a pass word and at least one of fmt, clippy or test(s). A `No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass` clause is therefore routine; this is stated in the doc comment. Parts (a)-(c) are still required for such a reading. The producer reads code_health.rs:529 and steward.rs:622-623 and copies those strings verbatim into corpus cases, together with this reading's criterion 8.
decisions.reason: Finding 4. Tokenizing `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` yields `d`, `targets` and `p`, which a plain word list misses. Stripping flags and crate names fixes that, and adding `existing`, `no`, `unrelated`, `behavior` and `changes` covers the steward default (steward.rs:622, per the finding). AC3 says a routine criterion needs no direct-check clause.

rejected.option: Add `d`, `p` and every crate name to the stop list
rejected.why: Single letters in a stop list let unrelated criteria through.

rejected.option: Skip the whole check when every behavior criterion is routine
rejected.why: AC2 still requires parts (a)-(c) for every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion.

decisions.choice: `check_behavior_test_reading` is a new `pub fn` in surveys.rs. The error names the parts as `(a) gate order and stop gate`, `(b) reused existing function`, `(c) record kind or round-trip deliverable` and `(d) direct check`, gives one example clause for each, and ends by naming `check_behavior_test_reading`. The doc comment carries the root cause, the gate, the four parts, `Limits:`, `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended`, `expected 30% of newly refused readings` (an estimate, not measured) and the reason with `because`, `now asks` and `new required`.
decisions.reason: `check_reading_text` returns only the error text, not the check name (checks.rs:492-503, replay.rs:54-65). AC5 needs the `refuse:` line to name the check, so the name goes in the message. The doc sentences are what the `*_refusal_is_declared_intended` corpus tests read (refusal_corpus.rs:3090-3207).

rejected.option: Change `check_reading_text` to return the check name
rejected.why: That changes `ReadingCheck`, `BinaryChecker::parse` and the `refuse:` line format the replay parses (replay.rs:35-47).

decisions.choice: AC4 on real readings is measured by `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294), which `touches_reading_rules` triggers for a change under crates/. It runs the replay over the newest accepted records after each parsed report, and the loop sends the list and the share back to the producer (run/mod.rs:2282-2283). The verification hold (`replay_stage`, replay.json) reuses the measurement for the same tree. When the loop send-back shows a share above 35% (30% plus 5 points), the producer loosens no marker, label or stop list. It writes the measured share and the newly refused job ids into its report summary. The fixture replay test `behavior_test_replay_stays_within_the_declared_share` is kept. It is described, and commented in the code, as a mechanics test only. It shows that docs, feature and content-only readings are never newly refused, that the declaration parses to 30%, and that the hold rule applies. It is not evidence of the bound.
decisions.reason: Finding 3. The ten fixtures are chosen by the author, so the fixture result cannot say anything about recent accepted readings. The producer cannot read `records/` in its snapshot (system facts, producer snapshot), so only `loop_replay` and the verification replay can measure the share. AC4 says markers are not loosened and the share and ids are reported.

rejected.option: Present the fixture replay as proof of the 30% bound
rejected.why: Its result depends on which fixtures were picked.

rejected.option: Read accepted readings from `records/` inside a test
rejected.why: `records/` is absent from the producer snapshot.

rejected.option: Loosen labels or markers if the loop replay is above 35%

rejected.why: It breaks the count assertion and the 220-byte line cap.

rejected.why: Out of scope, and the reader budget is nearly full.

decisions.reason: Finding 6. The report field excuses a planned file (run/send_back.rs:252, run/mod.rs:1616-1633, run/producer.rs:456). status.rs groups refusals by the recorded rule string (status.rs:226) and names `check_code_survey` only as a test constant (status.rs:3908). verify.rs reads the generic replay hold (verify.rs:500-526). replay.rs needs no change because `replay_declaration` already parses the declared share (replay.rs:263-285). Changing them would be an unrelated change, which AC8 forbids.

The producer would see an unexcused planned file.

risks.risk: The real newly refused share may be above 35%. Most past code readings used a one-line survey, so every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion is newly refused. Using `Existing code:` for (b) lowers the share a little.
risks.mitigation: `loop_replay` measures it on real accepted readings during the producer's work. If it is above 35%, no marker, label or stop list is loosened, and the share and the newly refused job ids go into the producer report. The 30% is declared with the reason sentence the replay rules require above 25%.

risks.risk: Lexical skip-switch matching misses other names and prose descriptions. The directly-before negation refuses some honest phrasings, such as `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, and can accept a phrase that is only superficially negated.
risks.mitigation: The closed list, the negation rule and the pinned false case are stated in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG. Corpus cases pin accepted forms (`not through skip_probe`, `skip_note`) and refused forms.

risks.risk: The routine-criterion stop list may miss other wordings of a routine criterion, which would then need a `Direct check:` clause.
risks.mitigation: Flags and `athena-*` crate names are stripped before the list is applied. The producer pins the strings from code_health.rs:529, steward.rs:622-623 and criterion 8 in corpus cases. A refused routine criterion gets an error that names it.

risks.risk: Many reading.rs and corpus fixtures use the short survey and would be newly refused. A missed site fails the test suite.
risks.mitigation: The change is in two places: `code_reading` and the corpus survey helper. The producer lists the call sites in the dependents and runs `cargo test -p athena-core` and `-p athena-cli`.

risks.risk: Refactoring the three label filters could change a check that already uses them.
risks.mitigation: The helper keeps the same rule (trim, case-insensitive prefix). The existing tests for those checks run unchanged.

risks.risk: The reader brief section is capped by existing tests, so adding the sentence could break them if the bounds are not raised by the right amount.
risks.mitigation: The producer measures the guide growth and raises both bounds by that amount only. No prompt file is edited, so the reader budget of 1998 of 2000 does not move.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. Layer 1 (measures AC4 on real readings): the producer's loop runs `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) after each parsed report, because the change touches crates/. It replays the newest accepted records with the real `check_reading_text` on both builds and sends the share and the newly refused list back. The verification replay (`replay_stage`, replay.json) reuses it for the same tree. The producer reads the send-back (plan step 12). If the share is above 35% it loosens nothing and writes the measured share and the newly refused job ids into its report summary. Layer 2 (mechanics only, not evidence of the bound): `behavior_test_replay_stays_within_the_declared_share` in reading.rs, next to the replay tests. It calls `replay(&cases, &base, &candidate, declared)` from replay.rs. `declared` comes from `replay_declaration_of` on a Reading whose criterion 4 holds the AC4 text, so the real code parses the 30% and the reason sentence. The candidate is the real gate `check_reading_text`. The base is a closure that runs the same real gate on the reading with `CLAUSES` appended, and the test first asserts every fixture is accepted by it. The fixtures are docs, feature and content-only readings and code readings with a one-line `Code survey:` and a behavior criterion. It asserts the newly refused ids are exactly the code behavior readings, that docs, feature and content-only readings are never newly refused, that the declaration parses to 30, and that the hold rule is true with no declared share and false with 30.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes in the producer's loop and in `cargo test -p athena-core`. The loop replay line shows the measured share on real accepted readings. The share and ids come from the send-back, not from the fixture test.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new check the candidate equals the base, so the newly refused list is empty and the id assertion fails. If the check also refused docs or content-only readings, the id assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `replay` and `replay_declaration_of` (exist, replay.rs:263-290, 365) and `loop_replay` (exists, run/mod.rs:2294). The candidate is the production gate. The base closure runs the same production gate on a reading with clauses added, so the logic under test is not in the double. The fixture test is added by plan step 7.
